subject: Redwood Inference MSA: Liability carve-outs & SLA credit linkage

Cc: Ben Tanner <btanner@tannerlaw.com>

Subject: MSA redlines — Liability cap and SLA credits

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are Arcadia's redlines to the proposed MSA (see Redline_MSA_Arcadia_v3.docx) — our legal and procurement teams flagged a few critical items we need to resolve before signature:

- Liability cap: proposing a fixed cap of $3,000,000 (we'd prefer a dollar cap rather than an annual-fee multiple).
- Exclusions: carve-outs for data breaches and regulatory fines (we expect Redwood to retain responsibility where you are at fault).
- Consequential damages: we want consequential damages to be excluded except for direct damages.
- SLA & credits: Arcadia requires that SLA credits be available and that credits are the sole financial remedy for service levels, but we cannot accept credits as the only remedy for data loss / confidentiality breaches.

Please confirm whether Redwood can accept these points or provide your counter language. Ben (cc) is our outside counsel and will coordinate redline technicalities.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is aiming for signature within two weeks.

Best,
Amelia Reed
Director, Procurement — Arcadia Health

- $3M fixed liability cap (external wants dollar cap, not fee multiple)
- Carve-outs for 'data breach' and regulatory fines in their favor

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA redlines — Arcadia (liability / SLA credits)

Soojin / team,

I've reviewed Arcadia's redlines and ran the legal analysis — below are the material points and proposed positions:

1) Liability cap
- Redwood standard: greater of $1,000,000 or 12 months of recurring fees.
- Arcadia asks for $3,000,000 flat.
- Risk: larger fixed cap increases our tail exposure for low-revenue customers but may be acceptable for strategic healthcare accounts.
- Proposal: counter with a hybrid: liability = greater of $2,000,000 or 12 months of fees, with $3M available if Arcadia commits to a 24-month minimum spend (or a multi-year order form).

2) Carve-outs / exclusions
- Arcadia wants to carve out data breach & regulatory fines. We should narrowly define carve-outs to 'wilful misconduct' / 'fraud' / 'gross negligence' only.
- For security incidents, we can accept carve-outs for indemnity and remediation obligations but not unlimited regulatory fines. Suggest we accept indemnity up to insurable limits and require notice/cooperation.

3) Consequential damages
- Standard exclusion (we should keep). Arcadia's request to exclude consequential damages is fine, but ensure 'consequential' is defined as in our template (no indirect losses).

4) SLA credits & sole remedy
- Arcadia wants credits as the sole financial remedy for service-level failures. We agree that credits can be the exclusive financial remedy for latency/availability issues, but they cannot be the sole remedy for security/data incidents or for breaches of confidentiality.
- Practical language: "For performance-related failures under the SLA, Customer's exclusive financial remedy shall be service credits up to the cap specified in the SLA. This exclusive financial remedy shall not apply to claims arising from Redwood's breach of confidentiality obligations, data security incidents, or Redwood's wilful misconduct or gross negligence."
- Credit cap: recommend keeping credit cap at 100% of monthly fees (or a 3x monthly cap only if tied to contractual committed spend).

5) Recommended next steps
- Commercial: ask for a short note on whether Arcadia can increase committed spend to secure a higher liability cap.
- Finance: Laura to run exposure modelling for $1M vs $2M vs $3M.
- Legal: I'll draft the compromise language and send a redline.

I'll attach a proposed redline shortly.

-Markus

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Reed <amelia.reed@arcadiahealth.com>, Jordan Li <jordan.li@arcadiahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Tanner <btanner@tannerlaw.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposal: Liability cap & SLA credit carve-outs (Arcadia / Redwood)

Hi Amelia / Jordan,

Thanks for the redlines and for the quick review. We discussed internally and want to propose the following compromise to keep momentum:

- Liability cap: provide a hybrid cap — greater of $2,000,000 or 12 months of recurring fees. If Arcadia can commit to a 24-month minimum spend on the Order Form, we can increase the cap to $3,000,000.
- Exclusions: we will keep consequential damages excluded. We will not accept a blanket carve-out that removes Redwood's responsibility for data breaches. Instead: Redwood will accept indemnity and remediation obligations for security incidents caused by Redwood, subject to our insurance limits and with notice/cooperation requirements.
- SLA credits / sole remedy: For performance (latency/availability) failures the credit regime will be the exclusive financial remedy, capped at 100% of the monthly fee (i.e., one month's fees). However, this exclusivity does not apply to confidentiality/data-security breaches, regulatory fines, or willful misconduct — for those, the full suite of remedies remains available.

If that structure is acceptable in principle, Markus will send a concise redline with exact language and we'll circulate a final version for signature. If you prefer the $3M flat cap now, we can explore a short-term commercial offset (one-time credit or price adjustment) to compensate.

Targeting DocuSign-ready agreement by end of next week if we can agree on language.

Can you confirm principle acceptance or let us know which points you want to escalate?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Subject: Re: Proposal: Liability cap & SLA credit carve-outs (Arcadia / Redwood)

Soojin — thanks for the quick turnaround and the pragmatic compromise.

High level: procurement is comfortable with the hybrid cap (greater of $2M or 12 months fees) and the 24-month committed-spend route to $3M, pending final legal review. Legal (Ben) will review Markus' redline language overnight. Two small asks from procurement:

1) Can we get the SLA credit cap moved to a 3x monthly fee cap instead of 1x? Procurement argues it better aligns with operational risk for health workloads.
2) Please confirm that regulatory fines remain subject to the indemnity carve-out language and that Redwood will cooperate with regulator inquiries (we assume this is covered).

If those two items are acceptable, we should be able to finalize and proceed to signature + PO. I'll confirm after Ben's review.

Onward — appreciate the collaboration.

Regards,
Jordan Li
Senior Procurement Manager, Arcadia Health
